Delivered outcome=partial: the question is not decided, but its three tightest classes are PROVEN impossible and the identity gap is pressed to exact new conditions. (1) (10,8) A-vanish (7,1) (tight 32=32): PROVEN impossible two independent ways: (a) an exact Fourier/Parseval contradiction - L7 forces |A0+A1| = 25 with both 5-sets, so sum h_hat^2 = 175 is forced but the odd parity of both Walsh transforms forces sum h_hat^2 >= 135+135-31 = 239 > 175 (the m=4 analogue computes need = lower = 7 exactly, matching its 512 real covers); (b) the complete enumeration of normalized Sidon 5-pairs finds ZERO pairs (backtracking validated = full brute force 5040 = 5040 at m=4, m=5 slice cross-checks, hill-climb ceiling 23). Coverage in the class is independent of the free parameter d1 (proven; machine-checked). (2) (10,8) D-vanish (8,2) (tight 32=32): PROVEN impossible by complete enumeration of the L7-forced equality configurations: 4,287,920 normalized Sidon 4-pairs (D0,D1), 112,560 with 1-invariant complement C, all 28,815,360 (pair, A0t-choice) configurations fail ALL THREE translated coverage lines simultaneously (fail_hist {('I','II','III'): 28815360}); coverage independent of the free parameter w (proven). The reduction chain is validated end-to-end at m=4: the four L3 lines and a DIRECT S+S = F2^5 test agree on all 4,096 analogue configurations (512 covers accepted by both routes). (3) (12,6) A-vanish (6,0) (full odd half, 36 pairs excess 4): PROVEN impossible - complete transversal walk over all 169,911 normalized 6-sets D of F2^5 finds ZERO 6-sets X with X + D = F2^5 (branch-on-uncovered search; positive control recovers real transversals at m=3), so lines (I'')/(II'') are unsatisfiable. Plus an exact multiplicity classification (PROVEN): any full-sumset 6+6 pair would have excess-4 pattern rho = 2+2 or 1+1+1+1 on an affine 2-flat; the patterns 4*delta_p, 3+1, 2+1+1 are PROVEN dead by exact Walsh constraints. (4) (11,7)/(9,9) identity gap: one bounded pivot on the cross-sum multiplicity identity gives PROVEN necessary conditions sum rho^2 >= 17 (excess 13) resp. >= 19 (excess 17) - excluding the all-ones excess pattern on both splits and the (2,1^11) pattern at (11,7) - but no contradiction: DEMOTED as an exclusion mechanism (the excess is too large for the rigidity that killed (7,1)); the row remainders 501/196 stand. No 18-point cover constructed; the gap 20 <= f(7) <= 24 is unchanged.
